Hi Simon,

I am Hal, the technical side of the team. You have waited far too long for answers, so rather than another holding note, here is what I can tell you on each point.

On the power supply, you are right and I am not going to argue the toss. The L.350-12 is the open frame version of that Mean Well family, an industrial supply with a live, neutral and earth screw terminal block that is designed to be built into an enclosure, not sat on a desk with the mains side accessible. The one that came with your Gamma is the enclosed version with an IEC C14 inlet, which is why that one is fine as it sits. There is nothing you can do at your end that makes the open frame one acceptable, so please do not run it as wired. Whether the supplier can provide the IEC style module for the BS-2 is a buying decision rather than a technical one, so I have put it in front of Georges and Abel with your order number. A colleague is picking that up today and the answer comes back to you in this thread.

On the noise, there is some good news. The L.350 is convection cooled and has no fan in it at all, so what you are hearing is not the power supply. It is the BS-2's own radiator fan following its temperature curve: the chips heat the loop, the fan ramps to full, the water temperature comes back down, the fan drops off, and the cycle repeats. That gap between the ramp up and ramp down points in the stock curve is exactly your 10 minutes quiet, 5 minutes loud. Harlo OS gives you a manual fan percentage and a custom curve, so you can pin it at a steady medium speed and lose the swing entirely. That alone is worth the flash on a desk unit.

On flashing and rollback, the BS-2 is on the supported list now. The flasher runs in the browser at harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge, with a USB data cable, and it offers two install types: OTA keeps your settings, factory wipes them. Because it writes the whole image, going back is the same operation in reverse, done with the Bitfortun factory image rather than the Harlo one. I have asked JD for the exact BS-2 factory image file so you have the rollback in hand before you start, instead of hunting for it afterwards. I have also asked him to confirm whether the shipped Bitfortun build has any in place update in its web interface the way AxeOS does, because I would rather give you his answer than my guess. The certain route today is the USB flash.

On overclocking, the Danger Zone box unlocks chip frequency and core voltage. Two honest warnings first: your unit is rated at 8.5 TH/s, and running above that, including any turbo or boost mode, counts as overclocking, which runs it hotter and voids the warranty. If you still want to play, raise frequency in small steps and leave core voltage alone until frequency stops scaling, give each step at least an hour, and judge it on pool accepted hashrate and your reject rate rather than the number on the screen, which is self reported. Watch the water and chip temperatures and back off the moment rejects climb, because an unstable clock quietly costs you more shares than the extra frequency gains.

The B.1 manual in the box and the RGB fan buried between the radiator and the chassis are both fair points and I have passed them on as feedback to the people who pack and spec these.

If you want a faster line than email for the firmware side, the Harlo Labs Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD is @nullhashrate there. He is in it most days and answers BS-2 questions himself.

Thanks for the patience you have shown, and sorry it took this long to get a proper reply.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
